analysis.title: JPM US Market Intelligence - Morning Briefing (November 20, 2026)
key_insights: Pre-market futures are weaker with NDX lagging (SPX -0.4%, NDX -1.2%, RTY 0.0%), extending yesterday's AI unwind. Cited risks: capital/regulatory constraints, ROI doubts, and a wealth-effect/growth-risk feedback loop.
Pre-market moves: NVDA -2.1%, META -1.7%, AMZN -1.5%, AAPL +0.4%. INTU -9% after lower Q2 guidance, and the company announced it is selling Mailchimp.
Yesterday's pre-market rally fully reversed during the regular session. Week-to-date sector losses range from roughly 2% (Utilities) to 7% (Energy, Staples).
The AI debate centers on NVDA and the durability of AI capex in 2027 and 2028. A regulatory overhang across semiconductors adds uncertainty, with Trump's post-Asia-trip press conference at noon.
Treasuries rallied on a flight to safety while Fed messaging stayed hawkish. This week's Retail Sales and European inflation data did little to support the case for lower policy rates.
Yields are lower globally. UST is down 4-6bp across the curve, Bunds are rallying 7-8bp and Gilts 4-6bp, led by the front end, on weaker commodities and growth fears.
Europe: major markets are lower with the DAX and broader Eurozone lagging. Semis, Electrification, Momentum Long and Software are the worst baskets, Defensives were up 32bp, and ASML fell 5.7%.

Ron Adler (co-head of Global HT Trading): 'If everyone wants a clearing event, one might happen. If everyone needs one, it won't.' He sees no compelling reason to buy the tape given the rate trajectory, persistent inflation, decelerating 2027 EPS growth, geopolitics, slowing growth, a divided US government and hack/outage risk.

Adler says the day's trading was not divorced from the AI trade. Tech headwinds he lists are the NVDA overhang, possible chip export restrictions, tougher financing, fewer positive catalysts, and the impasse over 2027 hyperscaler spending, where both high and lower spending read as negative.
Desk flow was busy but nondescript, and the hope that the day would lift tech and the broader market was misplaced, at least for now.

The US Market Intel view (from the Nov 16 briefing) is Tactically Bullish. It argues positioning is cleaner and entry points more attractive, and that the AI build-out pace may be slower but demand is insatiable.

Bull case catalysts (Nov 16): NVDA earnings (capex reiteration, support for financing deals, clarity on leadership with a move to return Huang), capital markets deal flow ahead of the Jan 3 Congress, the JPM APAC Tech Conference (~250 firms), and Retail Sales. The recession basket (JPRECES Index) is +15.8% QTD vs SPX -1.2%.

NVDA flows have shifted from downside protection to playing for earnings surprises, with little fear of another downdraft (JPM Equity Derivatives). Hedge funds have been sellers for 6 consecutive weeks, a Positioning Intel record.

Bear case (Nov 16): another leg lower in AI/Tech, a fading incremental buyer (retail dip-buying and buybacks), a hawkish Fed narrative with 17 Fedspeakers this week and possible 50bp talk, and incomplete positioning purge. US positioning is ~20th percentile and global Semis exposure ~80th percentile.
Market pricing: 4 hikes (Dec inclusive). The note says a 50bp hike in December is highly unlikely, and views inflation as more of an early-2027 problem.

Monetization Menu (Nov 16): move back toward Tech with primary exposure to Mag7 and options to play an AI rebound. Prefer Cyclicals over Defensives ex-Tech. Likes Europe for Cyclical/Value exposure, though a stronger USD may temper outperformance. SPX earnings are tied to nominal GDP growth and margins are near record.
Dubravko reiterates a YE26 SPX target of 8,000 ($365 EPS, 21.9x), implying 8.4% upside from Friday's close.

Dubravko trade ideas: long 12M momentum vs short 3M momentum (essentially Tech vs Energy/Defensives); Low Vol less compelling after moving from 0th to 25th percentile (best within Low Vol: Healthcare, then Utilities, then Staples); AI Upstream attractive after the positioning flush; Consumer Cyclicals challenged by affordability, with longer-term value in Apparel, Restaurants and Retail vs Energy. Mortgage rates need to approach 6.0% to see Housing inflows.
Today's catalysts: UMich sentiment and inflation expectations (10am ET), KC Fed Services (11am), Fed speakers Waller and Cook, and earnings from BMNR, CPRT, IESC and VEEV.

Near-term catalysts: CPI (Dec 10), ISM-Mfg (Dec 1), ISM-Services (Dec 3), NFP (Dec 4), PCE (Nov 25, Dec 23), Fed date Dec 9, US government funding deadline Dec 11, G20 Summit Dec 15-16. The US-China trade truce is reported extended through Jan 20, 2027.

tension_points.theme: AI tech rebound vs another leg lower
tension_points.bull_case: Positioning is cleaner, with hedge funds selling six straight weeks. NVDA flows have shifted to earnings-surprise plays. Capital markets deals and the JPM APAC Tech Conference are catalysts, and demand for AI is described as insatiable.
tension_points.bear_case: NVDA may fail to reassure on AI financing, capital markets events may be delayed, and negative pre-announcements may come. Ron Adler says there is no compelling reason to buy the tape, and the 2027 hyperscaler spending impasse reads negative either way.
tension_points.what_invalidates: NVDA failing to reassure on AI ecosystem financing, a delay to expected capital markets events, or negative pre-announcements at the APAC Tech Conference.

tension_points.bull_case: Inflation is viewed as an early-2027 problem, and a 50bp December hike is considered highly unlikely. SPX earnings are tied to nominal GDP growth, with margins near record.
tension_points.bear_case: A hotter Retail Sales print and hawkish Fedspeak, possibly with several members discussing 50bp, would challenge the shallow hiking cycle priced at 4 hikes. Equity resilience to higher yields should not be expected to continue.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A hotter Retail Sales print plus continued hawkish Fedspeak with multiple members discussing 50bp.
